Generates a new token so the\n512\t   * installer flow can run again.\n513\t   *\n514\t   * Only TENANT_ADMIN / MODULE_MANAGER should call this (enforced by resolver).\n515\t   */\n516\t  async resetForReprovisioning(\n517\t    deviceId: string,\n518\t    tenantId: string,\n519\t  ): Promise<RegenerateTokenResponse> {\n520\t    const device = await this.deviceRepository.findOne({\n521\t      where: { id: deviceId, tenantId },\n522\t    });\n523\t\n524\t    if (!device) {\n525\t      throw new NotFoundException(`Device ${deviceId} not found`);\n526\t    }\n527\t\n528\t    //   * Use case: device was activated but lost its config (SD card failure,\n   * re-installation, config save failure). Generates a new token so the\n   * installer flow can run again.\n   *\n   * Only TENANT_ADMIN / MODULE_MANAGER should call this (enforced by resolver).\n   */\n  async resetForReprovisioning(\n    deviceId: string,\n    tenantId: string,\n  ): Promise<RegenerateTokenResponse> {\n    const device = await this.deviceRepository.findOne({\n      where: { id: deviceId, tenantId },\n    });\n\n    if (!device) {\n      throw new NotFoundException(`Device ${deviceId} not found`);\n    }\n\n    // SENSOR-MEDIUM-008: REVOKED is terminal — re-provisioning would silently\n    // un-revoke the device.\n    if (isTerminalLifecycleState(device.lifecycleState)) {\n      throw new BadRequestException(\n        `Cannot re-provision a device in a terminal state (${device.lifecycleState})`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Generate fresh provisioning credentials\n    const provisioningToken = this.generateProvisioningToken();\n    const tokenExpiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + this.TOKEN_TTL_HOURS * 60 * 60 * 1000);\n\n    // Reset activation state\n    await this.deviceRepository.update(device.id, {\n      provisioningToken: this.hashToken(provisioningToken),\n      tokenExpiresAt,\n      tokenUsedAt: null, // TypeORM: sends SET token_used_at = NULL\n      lifecycleState: DeviceLifecycleState.REGISTERED,\n      mqttPasswordHash: null,\n      fingerprint: null,\n      agentVersion: null,\n      isOnline: false,","numLines":40,"startLine":510,"totalLines":980}}}

\"tenant_repository_unscoped_read\",\n      \"verdict\": \"false_positive\",\n      \"judge_id\": \"aria-evidence-judge\",\n      \"model\": \"claude-opus-5\",\n      \"prompt_hash\": null,\n      \"confidence\": 0.86,\n      \"rationale\": \"Line 211 is `await this.deviceRepository.update(device.id, {...})` — a primary-key-keyed write, not a read. The row identity it uses comes from lines 189-191, `findOne({ where: { id: deviceId, tenantId } })`, which is the only read in `regenerateToken` and carries the tenant predicate; lines 193-195 throw NotFoundException when no row matches under that tenant. Therefore `device.id` at 211 is never a caller-supplied id: it is the PK of a row already proven to belong to `tenantId` within the same request, and the update can only affect that row. The identical shape (tenant-predicated findOne at 520-521, PK-keyed update at 541) is the file's convention in `resetForReprovisioning`.
